summary: Adds `loom factory close <order> --shipped-by <url>` so a human can mark a parked or stopped order shipped after finishing it by hand in its own merged pull request. It appends one `shipped` ledger entry carrying the URL and the approver (same source as `loom factory approve`), reusing the ledger's existing `url`/`approvedBy` fields; folds that URL onto `OrderState` so `status` can show it; refuses on any other phase or a missing/invalid order or URL; and reuses `Supervisor.ship`'s record-then-archive-then-remove sequence so a closed order's run state is archived and its worktree removed the same way, without ever calling GitHub. Because `dependenciesShipped` already checks `Phase == PhaseShipped`, a dependent order unblocks automatically once `close` runs, with no edit to either order.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Closing a parked or stopped order with `loom factory close <order> --shipped-by <url>` appends exactly one `shipped` ledger entry carrying the URL in `url` and the approver — from the same source as `loom factory approve` — in `approvedBy`.
After that entry, `loom factory status` shows the order as `shipped` with the URL in its detail column, and `loom factory inbox` no longer lists it.
An order whose `depends-on` names the closed order is claimed by the supervisor on its next pass, with no edit to either order.

Closing an order archives its run state and removes its worktree, in the same order as the supervisor's own ship: record the ledger line first, archive, then remove; if archiving fails, the worktree is kept and the command reports why.

`close` refuses an order that is running, retrying, waiting at a gate, waiting on a commit or PR approval, or already shipped, with exit code 1, the order's phase named, and an instruction to stop it first; the ledger does not change.

`close` refuses an order the ledger does not hold, or a `--shipped-by` value that is missing or not an `http`/`https` URL, with exit code 1 and a message naming the problem; the ledger does not change.
`close` never calls GitHub and never checks that the named pull request merged; the human running it vouches for that, and `approvedBy` records who.

`close` and the supervisor never both act on the same order: `close` reads the ledger fresh and validates the order's current phase before appending, the same TOCTOU-tolerant pattern `approve`, `stop` and `rerun` already use.
`templates/claude-feature-team/intake/README.md` documents when to use `close`: after an order parks and a person finishes the work in their own pull request, once that PR merges.

Every new or changed function has cyclomatic complexity below 7, every changed line is covered by a test that can fail, `go test ./...` and the lint pass, and no file outside `scope.paths` changes except this run's own delivery record under `docs/features/factory-close-shipped-by-hand/`.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: close must store and print the --shipped-by URL only; it must never fetch, open, or otherwise make a network call to it.
Each close call appends exactly one ledger line, written atomically, the same single-write guarantee Ledger.Append already provides for every other event.
close must not introduce a second way to approve or ship an order outside the ledger; approvedBy must come from the same source approve already uses (the operating system user).

affectedComponents.reason: Add Close, closeable and isHTTPURL beside the existing RequestStop/RequestResume/RequestRerun human-issued controls, following the same orderIn lookup and ErrNotApplicable refusal style.
Add an entryUpdates[EventShipped] handler that carries a non-empty Entry.URL onto OrderState.URL, so a closed order's URL renders in `status` the same way a normal ship's PR URL already does.
New unit tests for Close/closeable/isHTTPURL, beside control.go per the spec's Test Approach, covering every acceptance criterion and refusal path.
Add the `close` subcommand, its required --shipped-by flag, and runFactoryClose, wiring factory.Close with openLedger(), worktree.New(layout.Root) as the Repository, and approverName().
Add in-process command tests for `close`, reusing the existing writeLedger/claimedEntry/runFactoryCommand helpers that already stand up an order in a given phase without running anything.

dataModelChanges.description: No on-disk schema change: Entry.URL and Entry.ApprovedBy already exist in ledger.go. Only the in-memory fold in replay.go's entryUpdates map gains a handler for EventShipped that copies a non-empty Entry.URL onto OrderState.URL.

architecturalFlags: Close reuses the unexported archiveRun function already in finish.go (same package, internal/factory) rather than duplicating or exporting the archive-then-remove sequence — keeps the supervisor's own ship as the one place that logic is defined.

No new lock is introduced: close validates the order's current phase against a freshly read ledger before appending, the same pattern RequestStop/RequestResume/RequestRerun already rely on instead of the supervisor.lock file (which only guards a second `loom factory run`).

developer: In internal/factory/replay.go, add entryUpdates[EventShipped] = func(o *OrderState, e Entry) that sets o.URL = e.URL only when e.URL is non-empty, leaving the supervisor's own ship() (which appends no URL) unaffected.
In internal/factory/control.go, add isHTTPURL(raw string) bool using net/url.Parse, true only for scheme http or https with a non-empty host.

In internal/factory/control.go, add closeable(orders map[string]*OrderState, id, rawURL string) (*OrderState, error): look up the order via the existing orderIn, validate rawURL with isHTTPURL, and refuse unless order.Phase is PhaseParked or PhaseStopped, reusing RequestRerun's existing refusal text ('%s is %s; stop it first, or it has already shipped').

In internal/factory/control.go, add Close(ledger *Ledger, orders map[string]*OrderState, layout Layout, repo Repository, id, rawURL, approver string) (string, error): call closeable, append one Entry{Event: EventShipped, Order: id, URL: rawURL, ApprovedBy: approver}, then call archiveRun(order, layout.RunArchivePath(id)) and repo.RemoveWorktree(order.Claim.Worktree), returning a warning string (nil error) when either step fails, matching Supervisor.ship's own wording ('%s shipped, but its run state was not archived, so its worktree is kept: %v' / '%s shipped, but its worktree was not removed: %v').

In cmd/loom/cmd/factory.go, add factoryCloseCmd (Use: "close <order>", Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1)) with a required --shipped-by string flag, register it in init(), and add runFactoryClose that calls openLedger(), then factory.Close(ledger, orders, layout, worktree.New(layout.Root), args[0], the flag value, approverName()), printing the returned warning or a success line naming the order and URL.

In templates/claude-feature-team/intake/README.md, add close to the Lifecycle/Status material: use it once a parked or stopped order's work was finished by hand in its own pull request, after that PR merges.

edgeCases.case: The named order is not in the ledger at all.
edgeCases.handling: closeable's orderIn refuses with 'ErrNotApplicable: no order "<id>" in the ledger'; exit code 1; ledger unchanged.
cobra's required-flag check refuses before RunE runs, so the ledger is never touched; Close's own isHTTPURL check gives the same refusal if ever called directly with an empty value.

edgeCases.case: --shipped-by is present but not an http or https URL (e.g. a bare path, or ftp://).
edgeCases.handling: isHTTPURL returns false; closeable refuses naming --shipped-by; exit code 1; ledger unchanged.

edgeCases.case: The order is running, retrying, waiting at a gate, completed, committed, pushed, or proposed.
edgeCases.handling: closeable's phase allow-list (Parked or Stopped only) refuses with the order's phase named and 'stop it first, or it has already shipped'; exit code 1; ledger unchanged.
Same refusal path and message as above — PhaseShipped is not in the allow-list; exit code 1; ledger unchanged.

edgeCases.case: Archiving the run's workspace fails after the ledger line is recorded.
edgeCases.handling: Close still returns success (nil error) with a non-empty warning string; the worktree is kept; runFactoryClose prints the warning instead of the success line, matching Supervisor.ship's own behavior.

edgeCases.case: Removing the worktree fails after a successful archive.
edgeCases.handling: Close returns success with a warning naming that the worktree was not removed; the ledger entry is already recorded as shipped either way.

edgeCases.case: A dependent order lists the closed order in depends-on.
edgeCases.handling: No change needed in start.go: dependenciesShipped already checks state.Phase == PhaseShipped, which Close's ledger entry now sets; the supervisor claims the dependent on its next pass.

edgeCases.case: close runs while the supervisor is mid-tick on the same order.
edgeCases.handling: close reads the ledger fresh and checks the order's current phase before appending — the same pattern RequestStop/RequestResume/RequestRerun already use; a genuine race either sees the now-changed phase and refuses, or the supervisor's own next read sees the new shipped phase and stops acting on the order.
